Output ONLY one fenced ```json code block for Simple Host, and nothing else. Use this exact schema:
{"simpleHost":1,"name":"[YOUR-SITE-NAME]","files":{"index.html":"<the full, self-contained page as escaped text, with inline CSS and JS>"},"files_base64":{"assets/example.png":"<optional base64-encoded binary file>"}}
Relative links only — never a leading slash. index.html must be one self-contained file (inline CSS/JS).
Omit files_base64 when there are no binary files. A path must not appear in both files and files_base64.

SITE: [Describe your site in plain language here — what it's for, the style/colors/vibe, the font, any headings, and all the real details like names, dates, times, and locations. Say what visitors should be able to do.]

BACKEND — FOLLOW EXACTLY, DO NOT IMPROVISE.
This site is hosted at https://sites.simple-host.app/<handle>/<name>/ and has a real, free JSON backend that you MUST use.
HARD BAN: never use localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies, or any client-only/in-memory storage for shared data (sign-ups, RSVPs, counts, messages). Shared data MUST live on the server via fetch(). Do NOT invent endpoints. Do NOT hardcode the handle or the site name.
Pages may offer Google or sign in with email via auth.js. Writes accept a site session or any account's X-API-Key, identifying that account; invalid keys return 401 invalid_api_key. The page gets a site-scoped cookie, never an API key. Reads stay Origin-gated. GET /v1/sites/{sitename}/me and /v1/u/{handle}/sites/{sitename}/me report signed_in and expires_at (email and provider only on a custom domain; on the shared content host the page learns that the visitor is signed in, not who); anonymous responses contain signed_in:false and sign_in:"/v1/auth/oauth/providers".

RECOMMENDED — use the hosted auth.js helper. Add:
<section id="sh-auth"></section>
<script src="https://simple-host.app/auth.js" defer></script>
Initialize after the deferred script runs, e.g. in DOMContentLoaded:
SH.mount('#sh-auth');
The helper derives the site's API from the page URL. Do not hardcode the handle/site.

STEP 1 — Save an entry inside your async submit handler:
await SH.requireSignIn();
await SH.collection('entries').append({ /* entry fields */ });
await SH.state.patch({ops:[{op:'inc', path:'total', by:1}]});
Catch errors and keep the form visible. On error.code === 'visitor_auth_required', the helper updates the mounted sign-in box. Never claim success on failure. If append succeeded but patch failed, do NOT re-POST; show "saved, count will update" and retry PATCH only. For people counts use by:Number(guests).

STEP 2 — Live count:
async function loadCount(){ const s = await SH.state.get(); document.getElementById('count').textContent = (s.data && s.data.total) || 0; }
Call on page load, after saving, and every 4000ms; include an element with id="count".

RAW-FETCH FALLBACK — derive routes and send credentials + X-SH-CSRF:
const m = location.pathname.match(/^\/([a-z0-9-]+)\/([a-z0-9-]+)/);
const BASE = m ? location.origin + '/v1/u/' + m[1] + '/sites/' + m[2] : null;
const STATE = BASE ? BASE + '/state' : null;
const LIST = BASE ? BASE + '/collections/entries' : null;
const res = await fetch(LIST, {method:'POST', credentials:'include', headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json','X-SH-CSRF':'1'}, body:JSON.stringify(item)});
if (!res.ok) { const err = await res.json(); /* keep form; on visitor_auth_required offer Google or email sign-in; otherwise show err.error */ return; }
For sign-in, fetch providers from the apex /v1/auth/oauth/providers; if configured, navigate to apex + '/v1/auth/oauth/google?return_to=' + encodeURIComponent(location.href). Apex is location.protocol+'//'+location.hostname.replace(/^sites\./,'') on sites.*; otherwise https://simple-host.app. PATCH STATE uses the same headers and {ops:[...]}; GET STATE uses credentials:'include'. Never re-POST after a successful append.

STEP 3 — After a successful save (BOTH post and patch 2xx), hide the form and show a friendly confirmation message, then clear the inputs. Never hide the form on a 401 or any non-2xx. Never claim success unless both writes succeeded.

STEP 4 — Visitor messages/comments: do NOT hand-build these. Use Simple Host's built-in comments widget by adding EXACTLY these three lines immediately before </body>, and nothing else for messages:
- a <script> tag whose content is:  window.SH_COMMENTS={accent:"#HEXCOLOR", title:"YOUR TITLE"}
- then:  <section id="sh-comments"></section>
- then a <script> tag with src="https://simple-host.app/comments.js" and the defer attribute
(Only include Step 4 if your site actually needs a comments/message section.)

STEP 5 — Use a SOLID background color, not a gradient (the comments widget reads light/dark from a solid background; a gradient breaks it). The backend store is PUBLIC — never put secrets in it.

STEP 6 — A PLACE TO VIEW WHAT'S COLLECTED (do this WHENEVER the site saves entries — RSVPs, sign-ups, messages, orders). A form with nowhere to read the results is useless, so ALWAYS add a SECOND file "admin.html" to the files{} map (files can hold more than one file):
- admin.html derives BASE/LIST/STATE from location.pathname the SAME way, then does GET LIST + '?limit=200' and renders EVERY entry in a clean table (all fields, newest first) plus the live total from STATE. Load on open and refresh every 5000ms. Response shape: { items:[ { id, data:{...your fields}, created_at } ], next }.
- Match the site's visual style. Put <meta name="robots" content="noindex"> in its <head>. Do NOT build a fake password gate (the data is public by URL — say so in one small line rather than pretending it's locked).
- From index.html, link to it quietly: a small "Organizer view →" link (href="admin.html") in the footer.

ANALYTICS — INFORMATIONAL, BUILD NOTHING FOR IT. Traffic is counted server-side from the access log: never add a hit counter, beacon, or analytics script to the page. Two read-only owner endpoints, X-API-Key, owner-scoped, days defaults to 30 (clamped 1..365):
GET /v1/sites/<name>/analytics?days=30 → {range_days, classified_from, totals, last_24h, daily:[{day,...}], hourly:[{hour,...}]}. daily is zero-filled dense over the window; hourly is always 24 buckets ending with the hour in progress.
GET /v1/analytics/sites?days=30 → {range_days, sites:[{name,...}]} — every site you own, ordered by person.views descending. Admins only may add &all=1 for every site on the box; anyone else gets 403.
PATCH /v1/sites/<name> with {"name":"new-name"} renames a site and moves its files. A custom domain stays attached. The old public URL returns 404; use site_url from the response.
POST /v1/me/api-key/rotate returns a new api_key and invalidates the old key immediately. Update the agent or CLI with the new key.
Every bucket (totals, last_24h, each daily, each hourly, each site) is the SAME four-class split — person, bot, infra, unknown — each {views, visitors}. There is NO top-level views or visitors.
person = no automation signature; READ THIS AS THE AUDIENCE NUMBER. bot = crawlers, AI scrapers, SEO tools, security scanners, HTTP libraries. infra = uptime probes and health checks, usually the biggest number and never audience. unknown = days recorded before traffic was classified; report it separately, never folded into the other three.
visitors = distinct hashed IPs over the window asked for, so totals.*.visitors is NOT the sum of the daily figures (one person on five days = 1 in totals, 5 in daily). Views count 200/304 GET document responses only, for every class alike.

SELF-CHECK before you answer: (a) zero uses of localStorage/sessionStorage/cookies anywhere; (b) use SH.collection().append, SH.state.patch and SH.state.get (or equivalent POST/PATCH/GET fetch calls); (c) if used, the three comments lines are present verbatim; (d) the helper derives routes, or BASE/STATE/LIST are derived from location.pathname + location.origin, never hardcoded; (e) background is a solid color; (f) if the site collects anything, files{} ALSO contains admin.html that GETs LIST and renders the entries, linked from index.html; (g) writes send credentials + X-SH-CSRF; (h) a 401 with code visitor_auth_required keeps the form and offers sign-in; (i) POST-ok / PATCH-fail does not re-POST. If any check fails, fix it before outputting. Output only the JSON block.


EMAIL SIGN-IN — SH.email.request(email) POSTs to the site-scoped /visitor/auth and resolves {message,email,expires_in_seconds:900}. SH.email.verify(email, code) POSTs to /visitor/auth/verify with X-SH-CSRF: 1, clears the cached /me result, and resolves {signed_in:true,expires_at} (email and provider:"email" only off the shared content host). Both include credentials. SH.mount renders Google plus an inline email form, then a 6-digit code form; successful verification re-renders signed in. Errors appear in the box. Accounts are created lazily. Page sign-in mail contains no dashboard magic link and verification never returns an API key.

AGENT SAVING ON BEHALF OF A PERSON — POST /v1/auth {"email":"person@example.com"} → person reads the 6-digit code from their inbox → POST /v1/auth/verify {"email":"person@example.com","code":"123456"} → receive api_key → send X-API-Key on state/collections writes to any site. The account is created if missing. This key is that person's identity: keep it secret, never put it in page HTML.
